note: WIST-3 §3.4, §7 and §8: a Consumer resuming from a Snapshot authenticates the state file's `aggregator_key` tuples from the Anchor's genesis key before it uses any of them, and verifies the Snapshot index, the manifest and the state file under the keys valid at the height of the Checkpoint it adopts. `history` is one Log with its own Anchor, genesis key and cumulative tree; `epochs` are in Log order and each carries the Checkpoint the Aggregator published. A case is one Snapshot of that Log: `epoch_number` is the Epoch it is taken at, `checkpoint` the Checkpoint of that Epoch it is served with, `adopted_head` the height of the Checkpoint the Consumer adopts, and `index`, `manifest` and `state` the three unsealed documents. `expected` is `accept` with the key_ids valid at the adopted head, or `WIST3-E04`, the one code every rejection here carries. `violations` says which requirement the case isolates: the §7 rules of 1 through 5 the tuples break, the catch-up clauses `consumer_registry` falsifies — `omitted` for a key the registry holds and no tuple names, `disagrees` for a tuple contradicting the registry up to its verified head, `unknown` for a tuple the registry does not hold whose added height is not above that head — and the documents whose signatures do not verify at the adopted head. Those rule numbers and reason strings are this family's labels, not a diagnostic the protocol defines: an implementation replaying the family is compared on the accept-or-`WIST3-E04` outcome, the key_ids valid at the adopted head, and which of the three documents verify. `self_consistent` marks a Snapshot whose Checkpoint and documents all verify under the tuples it carries, so that the chain to the Anchor is the only thing rejecting it. `state_digest` is §7's digest over the case's own tuples; rules 1 through 5 test neither the sealing heights a tuple asserts nor which of two removals accepted in one Epoch it carries, and `removal_tie_break` is where the second of those is falsified instead — by the digest a replaying Consumer rebuilds. `mirror_cases` carry §5's Mirror list, which has no error code when it does not verify.

history.name: rotation
history.note: One Log whose Entries are key acts alone: the genesis key admits a successor at Epoch 0 and is removed at Epoch 1, two further keys are admitted at Epochs 2 and 3, and Epoch 4 accepts two removals of one key. Every Snapshot below is taken at one of these Epochs and read at one of these heights.

acts.subject: test-snap-b
acts.why: an accepted addition under the genesis key, read at height -1 where the genesis key alone is valid

epochs.why: the genesis key admits the successor that signs every later Checkpoint and unsealed document

acts.subject: test-snap-g
acts.why: the successor removes the genesis key, a key act read at height 0 where both are valid

epochs.why: the genesis key is removed: no document a Consumer adopts a head at or above this Epoch for verifies under it again

acts.subject: test-snap-d
acts.why: an accepted addition under the key valid at height 1

epochs.why: a key admitted above the Snapshots taken at Epochs 0 and 1, which their tuples therefore cannot name

acts.subject: test-snap-c
acts.why: an accepted addition under the key valid at height 2

epochs.why: a second key admitted above those Snapshots; a Consumer that walks to this height learns it from this Epoch's key act

acts.subject: test-snap-d
acts.why: one of two removals naming test-snap-d in this Epoch

acts.subject: test-snap-d
acts.why: the other removal naming test-snap-d; it is accepted too and changes no key registry state

epochs.why: two removals of one valid key in one Epoch: both are accepted and the §7 tuple carries the one at the lower Entry index

cases.name: resume across a key addition
cases.why: the Snapshot is taken at the Epoch that admitted the key its documents are signed under, and the Consumer adopts a head two Epochs above it

cases.name: resume after the genesis key's removal
cases.why: every document is signed by the key admitted below the removal; the removed genesis key keeps its tuple, now carrying its removing act

cases.name: a forged Snapshot whose key admits itself
cases.why: the attacker's key is named by a tuple, its adding act is signed by itself, and every document and the Checkpoint verify under it; rule 5 asks for a signer valid at the act's height minus one, where only the genesis key is, so nothing admits the key

cases.name: a forged Snapshot whose key carries no adding act
cases.why: a second tuple with a `null` adding act: rule 2 admits exactly one, the Anchor's genesis key

cases.name: a forged Snapshot restating the genesis key's public key
cases.why: one tuple, naming the Anchor's genesis key_id under the attacker's public key, with every document and the Checkpoint signed under it; only rule 2's comparison against the Anchor catches it

cases.name: two tuples naming one key_id
cases.why: the second tuple's act names its own key_id and public key and is signed by the genesis key, so only rule 1 rejects it

cases.name: two tuples whose keys share a note key ID
cases.why: one public key under two key_ids: a Checkpoint signature line would name both (§3.4)

cases.name: the genesis tuple states an added height other than 0
cases.why: rule 2 fixes the genesis key's added height at 0 whatever its Anchor signature proves

cases.name: an adding act whose public_key is not the tuple's
cases.why: the act the genesis key signed admits another key than the tuple names

cases.name: an adding act whose key_id is not the tuple's
cases.why: the tuple renames the key the act admits

cases.name: an added height above the Snapshot's Epoch
cases.why: a key admitted at Epoch 3 cannot be state at Epoch 2; the Consumer learns it by walking, not from a tuple

cases.name: an aggregator_key_remove carried as an adding act
cases.why: rule 3 reads the act's action, not only its signature

cases.name: a removed height equal to the added height
cases.why: a removal is above its addition for every key but the genesis key

cases.name: a removed height above the Snapshot's Epoch
cases.why: a removal sealed at Epoch 4 is not state at Epoch 3

cases.name: a removing act naming another key
cases.why: the act retires a key_id the tuple does not name

cases.name: a removing act beside a null removed height
cases.why: §7 makes the removing act `null` exactly when the removed height is, and rule 4's bound on the removed height has nothing to hold of `null`

cases.name: a removed height beside a null removing act
cases.why: the converse: a tuple asserting a removal carries the act that made it

cases.name: an act signed by a key added at the act's own height
cases.why: the signer's tuple admits it at the height it signs, where §3.4 reads the previous height's keys

cases.name: an act signed by a key removed below the act's height
cases.why: the genesis key was removed at Epoch 1 and the act reads height 1

cases.name: an act whose signature does not verify
cases.why: the Envelope still passes WIST-4 §5.1's field validation, so rule 5 is the only rule that reads the signature

cases.name: the index signed by a key removed at the adopted head
cases.why: the key is valid at the Snapshot's Epoch and removed at the Epoch the Consumer adopts, which the walk from the Snapshot reaches

cases.name: the index signed by a key added above the Snapshot's Epoch
cases.why: no tuple names the key; the Consumer authenticates it from the key acts of the Epochs it walks and it is valid at the adopted head

cases.name: the index signature failing under the key its tuple names
cases.why: the signer is valid at the adopted head and the signature verifies at no height

cases.name: the manifest signed by a key removed at the adopted head
cases.why: the key is valid at the Snapshot's Epoch and removed at the Epoch the Consumer adopts, which the walk from the Snapshot reaches

cases.name: the manifest signed by a key added above the Snapshot's Epoch
cases.why: no tuple names the key; the Consumer authenticates it from the key acts of the Epochs it walks and it is valid at the adopted head

cases.name: the manifest signature failing under the key its tuple names
cases.why: the signer is valid at the adopted head and the signature verifies at no height

cases.name: the state signed by a key removed at the adopted head
cases.why: the key is valid at the Snapshot's Epoch and removed at the Epoch the Consumer adopts, which the walk from the Snapshot reaches

cases.name: the state signed by a key added above the Snapshot's Epoch
cases.why: no tuple names the key; the Consumer authenticates it from the key acts of the Epochs it walks and it is valid at the adopted head

cases.name: the state signature failing under the key its tuple names
cases.why: the signer is valid at the adopted head and the signature verifies at no height

cases.name: a tuple disagreeing with the Consumer's registry below its head
cases.why: the Consumer's registry holds the genesis key as removed, so the tuple carries that removed height and removing act or the Snapshot is rejected; this one omits the removal altogether

cases.name: a Snapshot omitting a key the Consumer's registry holds
cases.why: every key the registry holds has a tuple, and this key was admitted at a height the Consumer has already walked

cases.name: a tuple for a key the Consumer's registry does not hold
cases.why: the tuple is admitted at or below the Consumer's verified head, where its own replay never saw the key; the tuples and the registry disagree about a height the Consumer has walked, whichever is wrong

cases.name: a Consumer registry the tuples agree with
cases.why: the one surplus tuple names a key admitted above the Consumer's verified head, which its registry says nothing about

cases.name: the tuple carries the removal at the lower Entry index
cases.why: the removal §7 names, and the state_digest a replaying Consumer recomputes at this tree size

cases.name: the tuple carries the removal at the higher Entry index
cases.why: both removals were accepted, so rules 1 through 5 read this tuple as they read the one above; the state_digest is what separates them, and it is not the digest a replay leaves

removal_tie_break.accepted_case: the tuple carries the removal at the lower Entry index
removal_tie_break.alternate_case: the tuple carries the removal at the higher Entry index
removal_tie_break.why: WIST-3 §7: of two removals of one key accepted in one Epoch the tuple carries the one at the lower Entry index, and rules 1 through 5 do not test which one a tuple carries. Both Envelopes satisfy those rules, and the two state files have different state_digests, so the digest a replaying Consumer rebuilds at this tree size is what falsifies the other one (`WIST3-E04`).

mirror_cases.name: signed by a key valid at the adopted head
mirror_cases.why: the list verifies, and §6.1 still lets a Consumer fetch from a source it names nothing about

mirror_cases.name: signed by a key removed at the adopted head
mirror_cases.why: §5 gives an unverifiable Mirror list no error code: its entries stay location hints

mirror_cases.name: read before the Consumer has a head
mirror_cases.why: §5's other unverifiable case: no adopted head means no key set to judge the signature under, and still no error code
